summary:
Your volume is essentially locked in place — 127 km over the last four weeks against 125 km the prior block, with the same run count both periods. That's not stagnation; it's a stable platform following the 44 km effort on June 8th, and the two back-to-back runs this week (11.73 km Monday, 13.77 km today) suggest you're managing recovery load deliberately rather than coasting.

Today's 13.77 km at 5:48/km with HR 137 is your cleanest aerobic efficiency data point in recent weeks — substantially lower heart rate than the June 20th run (156 bpm at 5:35/km) and Monday's effort (143 bpm at 5:59/km), while covering more ground at a comparable or better pace. That's a meaningful within-week signal. The June 27th session remains the standout of the block: 15.73 km at 4:49/km with HR 161 is threshold-adjacent territory and sits well above your recent easy-day baseline — worth tracking whether that kind of effort becomes reproducible or remains an outlier.

Your lactate threshold is pegged today at 4:24/km at 178 bpm, which sits comfortably above your 10K and half-marathon PB paces, suggesting your current aerobic ceiling has headroom relative to demonstrated race outputs. That alignment is worth keeping in view as you build more threshold-range sessions into the rotation.
